mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact lets Alloy invent a state in which two AccessAttempts share a single AuditEntry — i.e., an audit entry has been re-bound/mutated. The injection forces such an instance to exist, so the append-only and 1:1-audit assertions must fail.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditNonUnique { some disj a1, a2: AccessAttempt | a1.audit = a2.audit }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this load-bearing fact removes the constraint that a Permitted outcome lies in a documented Allowed cell. The injection forces a clinician-on-GetAccessLog Permitted attempt (a denied cell in the matrix); LeastPrivilege and the role-specific FRs must find it.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_LeastPrivilegeViolation { some a: AccessAttempt | a.caller.role = Clinician and a.operation = GetAccessLog and a.outcome = Permitted }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact lets the envelope vary across denied responses. The injection forces two denied attempts to have different envelopes — the existence-leak the byte-equivalent 403 envelope is designed to prevent.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_EnvelopeLeak { some disj a1, a2: AccessAttempt | a1.outcome = Denied and a2.outcome = Denied and a1.envelope != a2.envelope }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removes the structural care-team requirement on permitted clinician access. The injection forces a clinician to be permitted on GetRecord with no matching CareTeamMembership, which is exactly the FR-004 / SC-010 violation pattern.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_NoCareTeamButPermitted { some a: AccessAttempt, u: User, r: Record | a.caller = u and u.role = Clinician and a.operation = GetRecord and a.targetRecord = r and a.outcome = Permitted and (no m: CareTeamMembership | m.ctClinician = u and m.ctRecord = r) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact lets the audit entry's recorded accessor/role/op/outcome drift from the attempt that produced it. The injection forces a recorded-accessor mismatch, which is exactly the misattribution pattern the assertions guard against.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditMisattributed { some a: AccessAttempt | a.audit.recordedAccessor != a.caller }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact allows the same ClinicalNote to be bound to two distinct AccessAttempts — i.e., a note has been re-pointed or duplicated, the structural shadow of mutation/deletion. The injection forces two attempts to share one note.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_NoteShared { some disj a1, a2: AccessAttempt | some a1.createdNote and a1.createdNote = a2.createdNote }
